title: Deploying Autoregia
summary: Build and run the unified container locally, verify the mount matrix, and read the logs — the standard local deployment path.
body:
# Deploying Autoregia

The whole system is one Flask server in one container. Deployment means
rebuilding the image and recreating `autoregia` — never editing inside the
running container.

## Prerequisites

- Docker running on the host.
- CouchDB up on `127.0.0.1:5984` (container `couchdb`, volume `couchdb_data`).
- `.env` present at the repository root (git-ignored; see `.env.example`).

## Build and run

```sh
make deploy-local
```

The target builds `autoregia:local` from the repository and recreates the
container with `--network host`, mounting `.env` read-only at `/srv/.env`.
The port comes from `AUTOREGIA_PORT` in `.env` (8081 on this host).

> Production uses `make deploy-server`, which pulls the GHCR image CI
> publishes. That path is reserved for the human operator.

## Verify

1. `curl` the mount matrix — every sub-system prefix answers 200.
2. `docker logs autoregia` — no tracebacks, all mounts registered.
3. Spot-check one write path (e.g. create a PBS entry).

| Check            | Command                              |
|------------------|--------------------------------------|
| Mount matrix     | `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' localhost:8081/pbs/` |
| Toolbox registry | `curl localhost:8081/ate/api/tools`  |
| Container health | `docker ps --filter name=autoregia`  |

## Rollback

Re-deploy the previous commit (`git checkout <sha>` then `make deploy-local`).
CouchDB state is **not** rolled back — schema-drifting changes need a
migration note before they ship.

title: Commit Workflow (Hooked Git)
summary: The staged-set ritual: authorize with xattr marks, clear the annotation and encoding policies, commit through the hooks, then set the real message.
body:
# Commit Workflow (Hooked Git)

Global hooks (`core.hooksPath`) gate every commit: authorization marks,
an annotation policy, and an encoding policy. The workflow is a ritual —
run it the same way every time.

## 1. Inspect and stage

```sh
git status && git diff && git log --oneline -5
git add <paths>          # never blanket `git add .`
```

## 2. Authorize the staged set

Every added or modified file needs the `user.checkin` xattr:

```sh
git diff --cached --name-only | xargs mark-for-commit
```

Deletions and rename sources are exempt; `mark-for-commit` printing
`Not found` for them is harmless.

## 3. Pre-flight the policies

- **Annotations** — `@WORKING`, `@FIXME`, `@QUESTION`, `@VERIFY` in staged
  sources reject the commit. Reword or resolve before staging.
- **Encoding** — UTF-8, no BOM, LF line endings. `dos2unix <file>` fixes CRLF.

## 4. Commit, then set the real message

The `prepare-commit-msg` hook rewrites `-m` messages, so commit loosely and
amend past the hook:

```sh
git commit -m "wip"
git -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null commit --amend -m "feat(sopcs): catalog shell"
```

- [x] Stage only intended files
- [x] Mark the staged set
- [x] Annotation and encoding policies pass
- [ ] `git log --oneline -1` shows the real message

## Why the amend step exists

With `-m`, the hook sees `COMMIT_SOURCE=message` and overwrites the text —
there is no exemption flag. A plain `--amend -m` is rewritten too; only
bypassing `core.hooksPath` for the amend survives.

title: Re-seeding a CouchDB Database
summary: Seeds apply only when a database is empty — regenerating a fixture never refreshes a running DB. Drop the database, restart, verify.
body:
# Re-seeding a CouchDB Database

Each sub-system's `Store` seeds its database from local `data/*.json`
fixtures **only when the database is empty**. Regenerating a seed file
does not touch a running database.

## When to re-seed

- A fixture was regenerated and the running data must match it.
- The database is corrupted or drifted beyond repair.

Check for non-seed entries first — dropping the database destroys them.

## Steps

1. Inspect what would be lost:

   ```sh
   curl -s 'http://admin:<password>@127.0.0.1:5984/<db>/_all_docs' | head
   ```

2. Drop the database:

   ```sh
   curl -X DELETE 'http://admin:<password>@127.0.0.1:5984/<db>'
   ```

3. Restart the owning module (or the unified server) — the `Store`
   re-creates and re-seeds the database on first use.

4. Verify the document count and spot-read one document.

## Cautions

- Test databases live behind `COUCHDB_DB_PREFIX` prefixes (`wos_test_`,
  `gis_test_`, `sopcs_test_`) — drop those freely, they are re-seeded on
  every test run.
- Design documents and Mango indexes are re-created idempotently at
  startup; dropping them is safe.
